moved.sentence: Name methods so a call site reads as a phrase, with a label for every argument after the first.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: call sites read as phrases, with a label for every argument after the first.

moved.sentence: Follow the conventions of the framework you extend rather than inventing new vocabulary.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: follow the extended framework's conventions rather than inventing vocabulary.

moved.sentence: Prefix every public class, protocol, enum and constant with a project prefix, because Objective-C has no namespaces.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the full scope (class, protocol, enum, constant) and the no-namespaces reason.

moved.sentence: Mark designated initializers (`NS_DESIGNATED_INITIALIZER`) and forbid inherited ones that cannot work (`NS_UNAVAILABLE`), so a half-initialized object cannot be built.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: mark NS_DESIGNATED_INITIALIZER, forbid unworkable inherited ones with NS_UNAVAILABLE, with the half-initialized-object reason.

moved.sentence: Report recoverable failure with a `BOOL` or object return plus an `NSError **` out-parameter, not with exceptions.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: BOOL or object return plus NSError ** out-parameter, not exceptions; the programmer-error note is kept too.

moved.sentence: Build with ARC (`-fobjc-arc`).

judged.note: Kept and strengthened to MUST: compile with ARC (-fobjc-arc).

moved.sentence: Do not call `retain`, `release` or `autorelease` by hand in an ARC file, and do not mix manual reference counting into a target by file-level flags without a written reason.

judged.note: Both halves kept at SHOULD NOT across the two rules: no hand retain/release/autorelease in ARC files, no file-level MRC mixing without a written reason.

moved.sentence: Declare object properties with an explicit ownership attribute: `strong` for owned objects, `weak` for back-references and delegates, `copy` for `NSString`, `NSArray`, `NSDictionary` and block properties whose mutable subclasses a caller could pass in.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with every attribute and its case: strong, weak for back-references and delegates, copy for the listed classes and blocks.

moved.sentence: Reach for `__unsafe_unretained` only where the compiler cannot express the lifetime, and say why in a comment.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: __unsafe_unretained only where the compiler cannot express the lifetime, with a comment saying why.

moved.sentence: Name your own methods with that rule in mind, because ARC applies it to them too.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD, with 'that rule' made explicit as the method-family rule (carried as the rule's note) and the reason that ARC applies it to your methods.

moved.sentence: Break retain cycles in blocks.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: break retain cycles in blocks.

moved.sentence: Wrap long-running loops that create many temporary objects in `@autoreleasepool { }` so memory does not grow until the loop ends.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the condition (long-running, many temporaries) and the reason (memory grows until the loop ends).

moved.sentence: Use `__bridge` when ownership does not change, `__bridge_retained` to hand an object to Core Foundation (you now `CFRelease` it), and `__bridge_transfer` to take a Core Foundation object into ARC (ARC now releases it).

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with all three casts and their ownership consequences (CFRelease, ARC releases).

moved.sentence: Never use a bare C cast between the two worlds in ARC code.

judged.note: Kept at MUST NOT: no bare C cast between Objective-C and Core Foundation in ARC code, with the compiler note.

moved.sentence: Design the Objective-C API so it needs no Swift-side fix-ups: declare generics on collections (`NSArray<MyListItem *> *`) so Swift sees `[MyListItem]`, and use designated nullability.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: no Swift-side fix-ups, generics on collections so Swift sees typed arrays, designated nullability.

moved.sentence: When the Swift form should differ from the Objective-C form (a tuple instead of out-parameters, reordered or renamed arguments), mark the Objective-C declaration `NS_REFINED_FOR_SWIFT` and write the Swift-facing API in a Swift extension.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the condition and examples: NS_REFINED_FOR_SWIFT plus a Swift extension for the Swift-facing API.

moved.sentence: Keep the Objective-C implementation as the single source of behavior.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: the Objective-C implementation stays the single source of behavior; the Swift API calls it.

moved.sentence: Use `nullable`, `nonnull` and `null_resettable` on properties, parameters and return types; use `_Nullable` and `_Nonnull` where the simple forms do not fit, such as `_Nullable id * _Nonnull`.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with every qualifier and position, including the _Nullable id * _Nonnull example.

moved.sentence: `typedef` types are not assumed non-null even inside an audited region, so annotate each use.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the reason that typedefs are not assumed non-null inside an audited region.

moved.sentence: A method documented to return `nil` on failure MUST be declared `nullable`, and a method that must never receive `nil` MUST say so in its signature, not only in a comment.

judged.note: Both MUST requirements kept in two rules: nil-returning methods declared nullable; never-nil parameters stated in the signature, not only a comment.
